cards.explanation: The answer is violence. The earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence (Genesis 6:11). Then verse 12 says all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways. That's not one corner of the earth, friends. That's the whole neighborhood.

The answer is False, and the word that settles it is “both.” God says, “Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.” That's the creatures and the earth together, in one sentence. It's a tiny word doing heavy lifting, friends.

The answer is an ark. God says, “Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.” That's a vessel with rooms, coated inside and out. The biggest thing I ever built was a tower of cookie boxes, and it fell over. Noah got a lot more instructions than I ever did.

The answer is floodwaters. God says, “And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life.” Then He says, “Everything on the earth will perish.” I think this one is heavy. But notice He tells Noah ahead of time, and in the verses right before, He gives Noah the plan for the ark (Genesis 6:14).

The answer is His covenant. God says, “But I will establish My covenant with you…” A covenant is a binding promise, and it lands right after all that talk of floodwaters. Noah hears the hard news and a promise in the same speech. I think that's worth noticing, friends.

The answer is his wife, his sons and their wives. God says, “…you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.” So Noah isn't walking in alone. His whole household is coming along. I think Noah was glad not to go in by himself.

The answer is True. God says, “Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.” They come to Noah. I think that's a relief for a man who already has a giant ark to build. If I had to chase down every creature, I'd still be out there with a net.

The answer is everything just as God commanded, and precisely at that. “So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.” I follow a recipe most of the way, and then I get creative. Noah doesn't get creative, he gets it done. That's a whole lot of instructions to carry out.

The answer is that the LORD found Noah righteous. The LORD says, “Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.” That's the reason, right there in the speech. It's the same Noah we meet earlier as righteous and blameless (Genesis 6:9). Short and clear, like a recipe card I wish I'd had.

The answer is offspring. God wants seven pairs of birds on the ark “…to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.” Offspring means the young ones that come after. The text says that's what the pairs are there to preserve.

The answer is forty. God says He will send rain on the earth “…for forty days and forty nights…” Verse 12 says the rain fell that long. My longest bake is under an hour, and I still hover by the oven like a worried neighbor.

The answer is False. Verse 8 lists “The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground” as coming to Noah. Clean and unclean both come. It's not a clean-only guest list.

The answer is True. God said in verse 4, “For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights…” Then verse 10 says, “And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.” Same number, same result. God said it, and it happened just as He said.

The answer is the great deep and the heavens. The water comes from BELOW and from ABOVE. Verse 11 says, “…all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.” Bursting fountains and open floodgates, friends, that is water coming from every direction at once. Then the waters keep rising until they cover the mountaintops (Genesis 7:19, 20).
The answer is the LORD. Verse 16 says, “Then the LORD shut him in.” Noah goes in as God commanded, and the LORD is the one who shuts the door. The verse doesn't say how, friends, only who.

The answer is that the ark is lifted high above the earth. Verse 17 says, “…the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.” Verse 18 adds that the ark floated on the surface of the waters. Nothing about steering is mentioned here, just the ark going up with the water.

The answer is over all the high mountains. Verse 19 says, “…all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.” That's no puddle, friends. Verse 20 adds that the waters covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.

The answer is perished. I'll be gentle here, because this one hurts. Verse 21 says every living thing that moved upon the earth perished, and God had said, “Everything on the earth will perish.” (Genesis 6:17) Birds, livestock, animals and all mankind are named. The text doesn't hurry past it, and neither will I.

The answer is True. Verse 23 says every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed, and “…only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.” That's a quiet, heavy verse. Notice who remained, though: Noah and those with him, still in the ark.
